subject: Clarify controller/processor split + SCCs for UK deployment — next steps for Order Form
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@agreena.health>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Controller/processor split for UK nodes — initial questions

Rishi,

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so our legal team can tidy the purchase path:

- Agreena plans to run a pilot in the UK region in Q3; requirement is that customer data for UK clients be stored within UK/EU jurisdictions unless otherwise justified.
- We're seeing the DPA draft refers to Redwood as "processor" for API requests, but some Order Form language implies joint-controller responsibilities for analytics/usage telemetry.
- SCCs: our counsel prefers you propose which SCC module you'll rely on and whether you will be the importer/processor for any cross-border subprocessors (particularly any US-based monitoring).

Can you: 1) confirm the intended controller/processor mapping in writing, 2) share which SCCs variant Redwood will execute under, and 3) send a redline of the DPA highlighting any clauses that map to transfer-impact/hosting-locality?

We can attach our redline once we understand your position.

Appreciate it — Tom

--
Tom Ellis
Head of Security & Privacy
Agreena Health
attachment: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@agreena.health>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2025 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Controller/processor split for UK nodes — initial questions

Tom — thanks for the clear notes. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

1) Controller/processor: For standard API usage where Agreena supplies customer data (customers = your end-users) and configures prompts/routing, Agreena is the controller and Redwood is the processor. The exception is if Agreena requests Redwood to perform product analytics that include derived identifiers for their customers; that flow is currently scoped as processor-only but we can add a narrow joint-controller clause for that telemetry if needed.

2) SCCs: Redwood intends to rely on the EU Commission standard contractual clauses (Module 2/Processor-to-Controller) where applicable and a Processor-to-Subprocessor addendum for subprocessors outside the EEA. We'll confirm exact module text and signatory posture in the DPA redline.

3) We'll send a marked-up DPA that highlights transfer-impact sections (hosting locality, subprocessors, KMS/HSM key residency) and an Order Form excerpt for any hosting-choice pricing.

Next steps: Laura (legal) will prepare a short redline + rationale. Ben (sales) should confirm whether the UK-local hosting add-on changes commercials for the Order Form. Can you share Agreena's redline once that's ready?

I'll aim to get our redline to you by EOD.

Thanks,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Sales (UK/EU)
Redwood Inference
attachment: none

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@agreena.health>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Controller/processor split for UK nodes — initial questions

Tom/Rishi — Laura here from Redwood legal. I've reviewed the current DPA and Order Form language. High-level legal notes (for Agreena and internal teams):

- Controller/Processor: Confirm Rishi's characterization. We will propose explicit language at section 2.1 that clarifies: Agreena = Controller (data subjects: Agreena's customers); Redwood = Processor except for telemetry where joint-controller status can be triggered only by express checkbox in the Order Form. This is to avoid open-ended joint responsibilities.

- SCCs: We'll propose the current EU Commission SCCs (Controller-to-Processor, as an addendum) plus a processor-subprocessor schedule. For UK data transfers specifically, we'll include the UK Addendum to the SCCs and a fallback transfer impact assessment (TIA) summary as an exhibit.

- Subprocessors: Redwood's current subprocessor roster includes: AWS (eu-west-2, London), S3 backups (us-east-1) for long-term retention (opt-in), and a third-party telemetry vendor based in Ireland. We'll flag the telemetry vendor as optional and include a checkbox in the Order Form to opt-in for telemetry-derived insights.

- Order Form commercials: Ben — pricing impact: enabling UK-local hosting (London-specific reserved nodes) + KMS residency increases committed monthly by ~18% for the initial capacity tier. If Agreena needs strict UK-only retention with no US backup, cost delta ~+27%. Need your confirmation for exact SKU mapping.

Action items I will deliver by EOD: 1) Redline DPA with SCC addenda + UK Addendum, 2) short TIA exhibit (1-page) that identifies residual risks and fallback mitigations, 3) suggested Order Form checkbox language to capture telemetry opt-in and hosting selection.

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Tom — quick commercial clarity from my side:

- UK-local hosting option (reserved nodes in eu-west-2) is available as an Order Form add-on. Pricing bands: Tier A (<= 10k requests/day) +18% monthly; Tier B (10k–100k/day) +14% monthly with minimum 3-month commit.
- KMS residency (customer-managed keys hosted in UK KMS) is supported via our partner HSM provider; one-time setup $5k + ongoing per-tenant fee.
- If Agreena requires hard-cutoff backups (no US replication), we need a signed isolation SLA and a minor uplift (as Laura noted).

If you can confirm target request volume and whether telemetry opt-in is required for the pilot, I'll produce the updated Order Form with the SKU selections.

Thanks all — useful. Attaching our redline to show the areas that triggered internal flags (mostly around joint-liability language for analytics and US backup retention).

Quick answers:
- Pilot volume: expecting ~8k API calls/day (Tier A).
- Telemetry: opt-out by default for pilot; we'll enable only for optional analytics deliverable later.
- Backups: we can accept UK local primary with encrypted backups in UK; cannot accept US replication for customer PII.

We're looking to close legal/Order Form next week. Laura — please review our redline and confirm whether your DPA updates address the telemetry/jurisdiction ask.
